result.title: Measuring and Predicting Image-Token Repair Boundaries in Vision-Language Models
result.comment: 16 pages, 7 figures, 17 tables; supplementary material included
result.summary: Degraded images make vision-language models answer wrongly. Using synthetic paired blur, noise, and low light, we trace which clean image states can still repair those answers from the vision encoder through the language model. In four encoder models, 12 to 23 ranked tokens recover half of the full-patch effect, whereas random orders require four to fifteen times as many; encoder-free Gemma needs 22.2 versus 53.1. Full-block repair expires at a model-specific language-model crossing. The matched reverse-direction intervention is algebraically identical to text-token restoration, so its gap from image restoration measures a redundancy band rather than an independent predictor. A clean-image gray-ablation crossing independently predicts held-out repair with 1.53-layer error, against 3.65 for shared depth. Gemma MMBench has the only large attention-to-repair point gap; Gemma GQA does not. Restormer provides a non-oracle consistency check on two models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究退化图像下哪些干净图像 token 或其内部状态能修复 VLM 的错误答案，追踪从视觉编码器到语言模型的修复边界，并检验层深度、注意力与冗余能否预测修复效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接考察视觉 token 对答案的因果修复作用、逐层作用边界及注意力结构，与视觉证据筛选、latent 内容使用和深度／位置效应高度相关，可供核查其修复度量及冗余带结论。
